name: Electrical Safety Checklist
description: An electrical safety checklist covering outlets, cords, GFCIs, the panel and alarm context.

items.text: Check that outlets and switches are not warm, cracked or discolored
items.note: Warmth or scorching signals a serious hazard — call an electrician

items.text: Confirm outlets hold plugs snugly without falling out
Install tamper-resistant outlets or covers in homes with children
Avoid overloading outlets with too many high-draw devices
Listen for buzzing or crackling and stop using affected outlets
Hire a licensed electrician to replace any damaged outlet
Test GFCI outlets monthly with the test and reset buttons
Confirm GFCI protection in kitchens, baths, garages and outdoors
Replace GFCI outlets that fail to trip or reset
Check that outdoor outlets have weatherproof covers
Ask an electrician about AFCI breakers for bedroom circuits
Inspect cords for fraying, cracking, cuts or exposed wires
Replace or discard damaged cords instead of taping them
Keep cords out from under rugs and away from foot traffic
items.note: Trapped cords overheat and start fires

items.text: Use extension cords only as a temporary solution
Choose surge protectors rated for your devices, not daisy-chained strips
Unplug space heaters and chargers when not in use
Keep the area in front of the panel clear and accessible
Label breakers clearly so circuits are easy to identify
Note any frequent tripping and report it to an electrician
Never open the panel cover or touch breakers and wiring yourself
items.note: All panel work must be done by a licensed electrician

items.text: Have an electrician inspect older fuse boxes and aluminum wiring
Match bulb wattage to fixture ratings to prevent overheating
Unplug small appliances when not in use
Keep heat-producing appliances clear of curtains and paper
Stop using any appliance that sparks, smells or shocks you
Give large appliances their own dedicated circuits where required
Test smoke and carbon-monoxide alarms monthly
Replace alarm batteries yearly and units over 10 years old
Keep a Class C or multipurpose fire extinguisher accessible
Know how to shut off main power in an emergency
Plan and practice a home fire escape route with the household

faq.q: How often should I check electrical safety at home?
faq.a: Test GFCI outlets monthly, inspect cords and outlets a few times a year, and have a licensed electrician do a full inspection every few years or when buying an older home.

faq.q: Can I download this electrical safety checklist as a PDF?
faq.a: Yes. You can print this electrical safety checklist or download it as a PDF and keep it handy for routine checks and for new homeowners learning their home's wiring.

faq.q: What are warning signs of an electrical problem?
faq.a: Watch for flickering lights, warm or discolored outlets, burning smells, buzzing sounds, frequent tripped breakers, and shocks from switches. These signs call for a licensed electrician right away.

faq.q: Where do I need GFCI outlets?
faq.a: GFCI protection is recommended anywhere water is near electricity — kitchens, bathrooms, laundry rooms, garages, basements, and outdoor outlets. Test them monthly using the built-in test and reset buttons.

faq.q: What electrical work should I never do myself?
faq.a: Never open the electrical panel, replace breakers, or rewire outlets and fixtures yourself. Always hire a licensed electrician for panel work and any wiring changes to avoid serious shock and fire risks.
